# H3 Editor

> A timeline video editor for MiniMax H3 that runs inside ComfyUI. Write shots, render them with their sound on your own GPU, and cut picture and sound together. Everything the editor does is an HTTP call, and an agent skill teaches the whole workflow. It needs no other custom node pack.

H3 Editor is a ComfyUI custom node pack under the GNU GPL v3.0, published on the Comfy Registry as `h3-editor`. To install it, run `comfy node install h3-editor` or search for H3 Editor in ComfyUI-Manager; or run `git clone https://github.com/igorls/comfyui-h3-editor` in ComfyUI's `custom_nodes` folder, then `pip install -r comfyui-h3-editor/requirements.txt`. Keep one copy: the two routes use different folders. Restart ComfyUI afterwards. It needs ComfyUI 0.43 or newer, with its built-in MiniMax H3 support, and about 54 GB of model files, which the pack does not download. The editor opens from ComfyUI's sidebar, at `/h3take/editor` on the ComfyUI server (by default `http://127.0.0.1:8188`). Renders run on that ComfyUI's GPU. So far it has been tested on one 96 GB GPU.

What it does: clips written as shots (what happens, camera, cast, speech, sound), drafts and finals of up to 1920 pixels or a size of your own (including partial draft finalization and hold-cache storage management), extensions, bridges and merges that hold the joined clips' own latents, a cast with view-tagged pictures and voices and a catalog shared between projects, a dedicated Sprites workspace (square 512x512 / portrait / landscape canvases, 39/56/73-frame loops, 8-way runs, idles and named actions, BiRefNet + H3DefringeMatte cutouts, lossless frame cache re-exports from 32 to 512 px in PNG and WebP with Animwright JSON, self-pin loop closure, and >= 4 MP MiniMax-H3-Image static props, paired state variants and character turnaround plates), a built-in managed Render Queue, sound lanes, VFX clips drawn by code, notes on frames, scores and checks for every cut (picture, sound and camera movement), writing shots with a language model, built-in H3 checkpoints plus any other, LoRAs, model patches from other installed packs, project zips and a Colab notebook for finals on a bigger GPU.

## For agents

- [Agent skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igorls/comfyui-h3-editor/main/skills/h3-editor/SKILL.md): how to plan shots, render drafts, review them, join them, read the cut scores, render finals and export through the editor's HTTP API
- [API reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igorls/comfyui-h3-editor/main/skills/h3-editor/references/api.md): the routes, the project model, every operation and its fields, replies and errors, the summary format, and lengths and timing
- [h3.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igorls/comfyui-h3-editor/main/skills/h3-editor/scripts/h3.py): the command-line client the skill uses, Python standard library only

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igorls/comfyui-h3-editor/main/README.md): install, the exact model files with sizes and sources, a first video, using the editor, keys and troubleshooting
- [Changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igorls/comfyui-h3-editor/main/CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each release, newest first
- [Models and quality](https://igorls.github.io/comfyui-h3-editor/models.md): the built-in checkpoints, adding any other H3 checkpoint with its own steps, sampler and scheduler, a smaller text encoder, picking a model per clip, a project's LoRAs and model patches, how finals are refined, and how LoRAs land
- [The nodes](https://igorls.github.io/comfyui-h3-editor/nodes.md): H3 Take and the pack's other nodes, for building your own ComfyUI workflows
